$comment: The skin's contrast policy. Every entry = one fg/bg pair (role × state) checked against WCAG thresholds. level: AA/AAA -> text thresholds (normal/large); UI -> SC 1.4.11 (3:1, non-text elements: borders, focus ring). severity=error blocks the build; severity=warn only warns.
$comment-coverage: This list is the contrast gate's DENOMINATOR: a pair with no entry is not counted, so until 2026-08-05 the policy was silent about 27 colours the library really paints (lesson-33). Point 7 of `check-tokens` watches it: every colour token a stylesheet paints as background, text or outline has to stand in at least one entry. Choosing the PARTNER stays a human decision — the machine sees that a colour is unmeasured, it does not see what it lies on.
$comment-partner: The convention for choosing a partner: text is measured against the surface it stands on; a surface against the text lying on it; a border against the ADJACENT surface — for a control with a fill of its own that is the fill (`pct.checkbox.bg`), while for a button filled across its whole surface the boundary runs against the page (`pct.surface`).
$comment-disabled: The `disabled` states have severity `warn`, not `error`: SC 1.4.11 explicitly exempts parts of inactive controls, and SC 1.4.3 exempts inactive text. The entry stays, because being exempt from a requirement is no reason to STOP MEASURING — the report is to show how far the disabled state goes down, rather than have no opinion about it.

checks.$comment: The one pair a veil can be measured in: not "is the veil readable" — it carries no text — but "can you see where the dialog ends". The panel and the dimmed page behind it are both dark in the dark theme, and the edge is the only thing that separates them. Measured against the veil ALONE, with its alpha ignored: what is really behind the border is the veil composited over whatever the page had there, and the darkest that can be is the veil at full strength. So the number is the worst case, which is the one worth having.
checks.name: UI: dialog panel edge against the dimmed page

checks.$comment: A menu draws the page's own surface, so its edge is measured against the page — the popover's reading, one component over. The row is measured against ITS OWN background rather than against the panel's, and the two happen to be the same colour today: the pair has to name what the row really paints, or the day somebody tints the rows is the day this entry stops describing anything. The text stands twice over, because a menu spends half its life with one row painted.
checks.name: menu — a command on its own row

checks.$comment: The panel paints a text colour of its own, and it is what anything a consumer puts between the rows inherits — a heading, a line of explanation. It is measured even though no part of the component draws text directly on it.
checks.name: menu — the panel's own text
menu — a command on the row the user is on

checks.$comment: A disabled command, on the same footing as every other disabled state here: a warning and not an error, because the greying IS the message. This pair happens to clear AA against the panel, and pinning it as an error would forbid the one change that would make a disabled row read as one (req-token-contrast).
checks.name: menu/disabled — a command that cannot be chosen
UI: menu panel edge against the page

checks.$comment: A popover has no veil under it, so its edge is measured against the PAGE — the surface it really stands on. The dialog's own edge is measured against the veil instead, and the two entries together are the whole difference between the modal and the non-modal panel.
checks.name: UI: popover panel edge against the page

checks.$comment: The whole of a tooltip is one pair: a panel with a sentence on it and nothing else. It stands here twice over — once as text on a surface, and once as the only measurement the inverted pair ever gets, since `pct.surface-inverse` is painted by no other component yet.
checks.name: tooltip — text on the panel

checks.$comment: A toast stands on the page with nothing under it — no veil, no anchor — so its edge is measured against the page, which is the popover's reading and not the dialog's. The difference is not cosmetic: this is the one panel here that can be the only thing on a screen the user is not looking at, so the boundary is what makes it a message rather than a smudge in the corner.
checks.name: UI: toast edge against the page

checks.$comment: The tone's two paints, measured one by one. The ICON is what a tone really is here, so it is held to SC 1.4.11 like any other meaningful non-text mark; the edge is measured against the page exactly as the untoned edge above it. Both readings are per tone, because a policy that measured "the tone" once would be measuring whichever tone somebody wrote first (plan 4.14).
checks.name: UI: toast tone icon (success)
UI: toast edge against the page (success)
UI: toast edge against the page (warning)
UI: toast edge against the page (danger)
UI: toast edge against the page (info)

checks.$comment: The action is the one thing on a toast that does something other than making it go away, and it is drawn as text rather than as a filled button — so it is measured as text (AA) and not as a non-text control (UI). The background is the toast's own surface and deliberately not the page's: the two are the same colour today and the entry has to name what is really painted underneath, or a skin that tints the toast leaves this measuring nothing.
checks.name: toast — the action

checks.$comment: The line between two sections is a separator and not the boundary of a control: what identifies a section is the heading on it, and whether it is open is announced by the platform rather than drawn by this line. SC 1.4.11 covers what is required to identify components and their states, which this is not, so it is measured at `warn` for the reason the disabled states are: being exempt from a requirement is no reason to stop measuring.
checks.name: UI: accordion — the line between sections

checks.$comment: The hovered heading is measured against the tint the hover paints under it and not against the page — the tabs' rule, one component over: the two are different colours the moment a skin gives the row a surface of its own.
checks.name: accordion — a hovered heading

checks.$comment: The marker says which way the section will move, and it is the only thing in the row that says it in a drawing. It is measured at `UI` rather than as text because it is a shape and not a letter, and as an error because the direction it points IS the state of the disclosure.
checks.name: UI: accordion — the marker

checks.$comment: The rail under the strip is a separator and not the boundary of a control: what identifies a tab is its text, and what identifies the CHOSEN one is the entry below plus the label pair above it — both measured as errors. SC 1.4.11 covers what is required to identify components and their states, which this line is not, so it is measured at `warn` for the reason the disabled states are: being exempt from a requirement is no reason to stop measuring.
checks.name: UI: tabs rail

checks.$comment: The hovered label is measured against the tint the hover paints under it and not against the page: the two are different colours the moment a skin gives the strip a surface of its own, and the entry has to name what is really underneath.
checks.name: tabs — a hovered label

checks.$comment: The edge that marks the chosen tab, against the page it is drawn on. This one IS a state of a control, so it is an error: it is the second channel the label colour alone would leave the component without (req-a11y-forced-colors).
checks.name: UI: tabs — the mark of the chosen tab

checks.$comment: The drawer's edge is measured against the PAGE and not against a veil, because there is no veil: a drawer is not modal, so what lies beside its border is whatever the application was already drawing there. That makes this pair stricter than the dialog's namesake rather than looser — the dialog's edge is measured against a surface the library itself paints.
checks.name: UI: drawer panel edge against the page

checks.$comment: A disabled stepper and a disabled control: warn, not error — SC 1.4.3 exempts inactive text, and the entry stays only to show how far the disabled state goes down.
checks.name: pagination — a disabled control

checks.$comment: The current page's edge is drawn over the page surface, and it is the same colour as the fill it surrounds — measured against the surface because that is the boundary a low-vision user needs to see (SC 1.4.11).
checks.name: UI: pagination — the current page's edge
UI: the filled part of a progress bar against the groove
UI: the filled part of a progress bar against the page

checks.$comment: The same reading as the slider's rail, and the same answer: what identifies a progress bar is the FILL, the groove is the road it travels, and no one grey clears 3:1 against both the page and the fill.
checks.name: UI: the groove of a progress bar against the page

checks.$comment: The third of the same family, and the one where the reason is strongest. A skeleton stands in for content that HAS NOT ARRIVED: it has to be visible enough to hold the space and say that something is coming, and it must not look like something a user can read or press. A placeholder clearing 3:1 against the page would turn a waiting card into a wall of solid blocks — so the requirement it really answers is the forced-colours one, where the box keeps its extent through an outline in the user's own palette.
checks.name: UI: a skeleton's placeholder against the page

checks.$comment: The sheen against the placeholder it travels across — this pair is the one above turned around (the page's colour on the border's), so it could not clear 3:1 even in principle. It is motion and not information: nothing is said by the sheen that the placeholder does not already say, and a band that cleared a contrast floor would be a flash on every card that is waiting.
checks.name: UI: the sheen of a skeleton against its placeholder

checks.$comment: The cross is the whole drawing of a functional control, so it owes the non-text floor (SC 1.4.11) — muted at rest is allowed to be quiet, not to be invisible.
checks.name: UI: chips — the remove cross

checks.$comment: The pill's edge over the page. Warn, not error: the chip itself is not an interactive component — the button inside it is, and has its own pairs above — so SC 1.4.11 does not claim this boundary. It stays measured because the edge is what keeps a chip an object when a skin flattens `surface-100` into `surface`, and in forced colours the border is the one channel left standing.
checks.name: UI: chips — the pill's edge against the page

checks.$comment: The silhouette of last resort. Warn, not error: the whole subtree is hidden decoration (0052) and SC 1.4.11 claims no part of it — but a silhouette a sighted user cannot see is an avatar that looks empty, so the pair stays measured.
checks.name: UI: avatar — the silhouette against its box

checks.$comment: The ring against the page — the chips' entry one component over, and here the border is load-bearing three ways: over a photograph the fill is invisible, over a flattened skin the box melts into the page, and in forced colours the border is the one channel left.
checks.name: UI: avatar — the ring against the page

checks.$comment: The chosen segment carries the state by its FILL, with no shadow and no edge, so the boundary that makes it an object is fill against track. UI and not AA: this is a non-text element under SC 1.4.11. Warn, not error: the label's own pair above is the primary channel and forced colours restores an outline, so a skin that flattens `surface-100` into `surface` should be told rather than blocked.
